title: The quickstart reads taps from textEvent, but taps arrive in sysEvent
claim: The Your First App page counts taps from event.textEvent and returns early when it is missing. The handle-input skill says presses on a text container arrive as event.sysEvent, and only scrolls arrive as event.textEvent.
actual: On simulator 0.9.5 and on G2 hardware, a tap arrives as a sysEvent whose whole payload is { eventSource: 1 }. textEvent is never set, so the quickstart handler returns before counting and the counter stays at 0. Reports disagree on hardware: one report on SDK 0.0.13 sees a text-container click event and then a sysEvent for each press, and the quickstart handler would count that click. The page still reads textEvent as of 2026-11-17.
impact: Anyone who follows the quickstart exactly gets a page that renders and ignores taps. The page is the first app most developers build.
workaround: Read presses from sysEvent with eventType ?? 0, as the handle-input skill does. If a text-container click can also arrive, act on only one of the two.

evidence.note: Nine taps on a temple of real G2 glasses gave nine identical sysEvent payloads and no textEvent. Same result in the simulator. Simulator on macOS 15.
On hardware, each press delivered the text container's click event with no eventType, then a sysEvent about 350 ms later. Even App 2.2.x, minor version not given.
One text container with isEventCapture 1. Each click arrived as a sysEvent only; textEvent was never set. Same on SDK 0.0.14.
